correctness.rationale: Four exact matching energies reduce to two equations. The outer maps are reflections and the central Hamiltonian flight derivatives yield the closed expression for µ. Transverse inequalities fix the strict sign of its denominator, proving sign(µ−1)=−sign(Theta). The degenerate energy equations imply a nontrivial local solution curve, and transversality promotes it to a real period annulus. A standalone rational checker re-evaluates 588 strict-crossing fixtures and a published cycle. The universal proof does not rely on finite sampling.

value.rationale: The source gives a sharp cycle-count classification but does not determine robustness, attraction/repulsion, or whether neutral cycles can be isolated. These are central qualitative questions for nonsmooth Hamiltonian switching systems. A single explicit observable from boundary crossing heights provides a uniform stability decision and eliminates isolated degenerate cycles across all center/saddle combinations, with a source example realizing repulsion.
